content.text:
## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 65a7383f98f831cf957630ed5750bf2ec7f249cf

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation approach:**
The fixing commit 16840bb bundles a large refactor ("removing round end data / prep for mid-round loading") together with an unspecified "Also fixes a bug." To isolate the actual bug fix, I traced the history of each touched file. `TickCounter.java` and the `GameSession`/`SlaveSession`/`AuthoritativeSession` round-end machinery it replaces only exist in two commits: it was newly introduced in `65a7383` ("Cleans up and simplifies the game's processing in the session") and only modified afterward in `16840bb`. So any defect in `TickCounter`'s design must trace back to `65a7383`.

I also checked whether the "instant round completion" behavior was a pre-existing, intentional pattern (older `GameSession` code initialized `currentRoundTime = ROUND_DURATION` / `currentTick = TICKS_PER_ROUND` at construction, so `update()` reported "round over" immediately, which is used to show the round-end screen right after loading). That older pattern always relied on `startNextRound()` being called to reset state for subsequent rounds — which it reliably was.

**(2) The specific change:**
In `65a7383`, this ad-hoc timing logic was extracted into a standalone, reusable `TickCounter` utility class. Its constructor was written as:

```java
public TickCounter(TickHandler tickHandler, int maxTicks, int tickDuration) {
    this.tickHandler = tickHandler;
    this.maxTicks = maxTicks;
    this.tickDuration = tickDuration;

    tickCount = maxTicks;   // <-- starts "already finished"
}
```

with the Javadoc explicitly warning: *"Creates a tick counter. Has to be {@linkplain #reset() reset} first to get used."* This means a freshly constructed `TickCounter` is not in a neutral "0 ticks elapsed" state but in an already-finished state, and any caller that doesn't remember to call `reset()` before the first `update()` will have `update()` return `true` immediately. `GameSession.init()` (also added in `65a7383`) constructs the `TickCounter` and never calls `reset()` on it.

Commit `16840bb` fixes exactly this: it removes `tickCount = maxTicks;` from the constructor and removes the now-obsolete "has to be reset first" Javadoc, so a new counter genuinely starts at 0 ticks.

**(3) Supporting evidence:**
- `git log --oneline -S "tickCount = maxTicks"` shows the line was added in `65a7383` and removed only in `16840bb` — no other commit touches it.
- `TickCounter.java` did not exist before `65a7383`; it is a wholesale extraction/generalization of logic that was previously inlined and always safe because `startNextRound()` reset it manually — the extraction into a general-purpose class introduced a self-consistency flaw (a "fresh" object claims to be "finished").
- This flaw is directly relevant to the stated purpose of `16840bb` ("in preparation for mid-round loading"): if a session/tick counter needs to be constructed mid-round (not from scratch), starting in an implicitly "finished" state without an explicit reset is exactly the kind of latent bug that would surface once that feature is worked on — consistent with the commit fixing a bug it uncovered while doing this refactor.

**Uncertainty:** This commit mixes a broad refactor with a small bug fix, and there is no external issue tracker reference available locally to confirm which exact hunk was "the bug." The `TickCounter` constructor issue is the most concrete, self-contained, and semantically verifiable candidate I found (a documented "must call reset() first" footgun that was silently never honored), but I cannot rule out with full certainty that the referenced bug was instead one of the smaller incidental fixes bundled in the same commit (e.g., a hard-coded `"Client"` log label in `GameSession.startNextRound()` that should have been `"Server"` for host sessions, which dates back to an unrelated earlier commit `8612722` and would not implicate `65a7383`). I'm moderately-to-highly confident in `65a7383` as the bug-introducing commit, but flag this residual uncertainty.
